REASONING:
Step 1 – Frame the project  
- Objective: Improve the effectiveness and coordination of selected public programmes to alleviate constraints to competitiveness and job creation (investment & export promotion, innovation, active labour‑market programmes, labour intermediation, activation of social‑assistance beneficiaries).  
- Scope & components: Four main components – (1) Policy planning, monitoring and coordination (PPMC); (2) Investment and export promotion; (3) Innovation (Innovation Fund, matching‑grants, Technology Transfer Facility, public‑research reforms); (4) Labour (NES reforms, ALMPs, cash‑transfer for social‑assistance beneficiaries). Part A uses results‑based financing (DLIs); Part B funds technical assistance and project management.  
- Delivery model: Results‑based financing (reimburse eligible expenditure programmes on achievement of DLIs) plus traditional TA funding.  
- Timeline: Implementation start 26‑Aug‑2015; effectiveness 15‑Jan‑2016; implementation end 31‑Mar‑2019; expected closing 30‑Jun‑2019.  
- Budget: Total cost EUR 352.48 m (USD 100 m); Bank financing EUR 89.5 m; Borrower financing EUR 262.98 m.  
- Key stakeholders: Borrower Ministry of Finance; coordinating agency Public Policy Secretariat (PPS); implementing ministries Economy, Education‑Science‑Tech‑Development, Labour‑Employment‑Veteran‑Social‑Affairs (MoLEVSA) and National Employment Service (NES); Innovation Fund; IMF (Precautionary Stand‑By Agreement); EU Delegation/IPA; World Bank team.  
- External dependencies: IMF programme, EU‑IPA funding, existing payroll & budgeting systems, external donor projects (WB CIIP, USAID, EIB/EBRD), macro‑economic environment.

Step 2 – Category sweep (risk identified with supporting text)  
Technical  
1. Lack of functional technology‑transfer capacity (DLI 4).  
Financial  
2. Fiduciary risk rated substantial.  
Schedule  
3. Potential procurement delays due to PPS clearance of evaluation reports.  
4. PPS lacks adequate capacity for Bank‑funded projects and procurement procedures.  
Stakeholder  
5. Weak inter‑ministerial policy coordination (identified as a major weakness).  
Political/Regulatory  
6. MoE investment‑export support system is complex, non‑transparent and agencies have overlapping mandates.  
External  
7. High public‑debt ratio (over 70 % of GDP in 2014).  
8. Poor investment‑climate ranking (91st in Doing Business, worst in construction permits & tax).  
Organizational  
9. Extensive ALMP data are not being translated into concrete analysis.  
10. Design of cash‑transfer for social‑assistance beneficiaries may be challenging.  
11. Non‑achievement of DLIs can trigger disbursement delays (re‑assessment procedure).  
12. NES procurement staff lack capacity for Bank‑funded procurements.  
Environmental  
13. Possible direct environmental impacts from Innovation component (Mini & Matching Grants).  
Organizational (labour)  
14. Very high caseload per NES case‑worker (200‑2 000 unemployed per worker).  
Political/Regulatory (social‑assistance)  
15. Very high tax wedge on low‑paying jobs; benefits drop by least one dinar per dinar earned formally.

Step 3 – Evidence filter  
All 15 risks are directly supported by quoted statements (≤25 words) from the appraisal document.

Step 4 – Assess & mitigate  

|Risk|Likelihood (1‑5)|Impact (1‑5)|Justification|Mitigation|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|R01 TTF capacity|3|4|TTF capacity currently insufficient; no entity with demonstrable transaction capacity.|Secure additional funding, recruit expert staff, fast‑track deployment of service lines.|
|R02 Fiduciary risk|4|5|“Overall combined fiduciary risk and financial management residual risk are rated as substantial.”|Strengthen internal controls, conduct regular audits, provide intensive FM training to PPS and ministries.|
|R03 Procurement clearance delays|3|3|“Potential procurement delays: arrangements for clearance of evaluation reports by the PPS may lead to procurement delays.”|Set firm clearance timelines, parallel review streams, Bank monitoring of milestones.|
|R04 PPS capacity gap|4|4|“The assessment concluded that the PPS does not have adequate capacity in Bank funded projects and with Bank procurement procedures.”|Hire experienced procurement/FIDUCIARY specialist, deliver on‑the‑job training, develop SOPs.|
|R05 Weak policy coordination|3|4|“Policy coordination is among the weakest points for Serbia.”|Formalise PPMC Working Group charter, schedule semi‑annual reviews, link KPIs to ministerial performance contracts.|
|R06 MoE agency complexity|3|4|“The system of support provided by the MoE’s agencies is complex and non‑transparent. The agencies have overlapping mandates, no coordination.”|Conduct agency mapping, define clear mandates, merge/restructure agencies, introduce performance‑based budgeting.|
|R07 High public debt|3|5|“Public debt to GDP ratio sharply increased … to over 70 % in 2014.”|Maintain fiscal consolidation, align disbursements with IMF targets, build contingency buffers.|
|R08 Poor investment climate|3|4|“Serbia ranks 91st … worst in Construction Permits and Paying Taxes.”|Support regulatory reforms, simplify permits, tax‑administration streamlining, monitor Doing‑Business indicators.|
|R09 ALMP data not used|3|3|“Extensive data collection … this information should be better translated into concrete analysis of the effects of programs.”|Create dedicated data‑analysis unit, train staff in impact‑evaluation, embed results in DLI reporting.|
|R10 Cash‑transfer design risk|3|4|“The cash transfer … will be designed … to make formal work worthwhile compared to receiving benefits.”|Pilot on a small cohort, involve beneficiaries in design, conduct feasibility study before scaling.|
|R11 DLI non‑achievement|3|4|“If a DLI is not achieved, a ‘request for reassessment’ may be submitted … must provide a justification and an Action Plan.”|Implement robust monitoring, early evidence collection, maintain buffer funds for partial payments.|
|R12 NES procurement capacity|3|3|“Staff do not have capacity in Bank‑funded projects and with Bank procurement procedures.”|Hire procurement specialist for NES, provide targeted training, use joint PPS‑NES procurement support.|
|R13 Environmental impacts from Innovation|2|2|“Direct, physical environmental impacts could arise … The main environmental concern deals with the Mini & Matching Grant Programs.”|Apply ESMF screening to all Innovation grants, require EMP where needed, monitor compliance.|
|R14 High NES caseload|4|3|“The average caseload varies between around 200 to over 2 000 registered unemployed per case worker across branch offices.”|Introduce active‑job‑seeker registry, re‑allocate staff, certify case‑workers, set caseload caps.|
|R15 High tax wedge on low‑pay jobs|2|3|“Serbia has one of the highest tax wedges on low‑paying jobs … benefits drop by least one dinar per dinar earned formally.”|Model tax‑benefit scenarios, redesign social‑assistance formula, pilot in‑work benefit for target group.|

Step 5 – Consolidate  
All risks are distinct; no duplicates remain. The register contains 15 material risks supported by the appraisal document.
